findings.title: `sq auth login` and `sq auth logout` spawn the Codex runtime but are not fully bounded by a timeout
findings.description: The design states spawning is confined to "a Codex turn, `sq auth login/logout`, and `sq auth status`" (Data Flow, Runtime startup cost). The D7 table bounds `handle.wait()` with `codex.login_timeout_s` and runtime start + `account()` in `sq auth status` with `codex.account_timeout_s`. But the runtime start that precedes `login_chatgpt()`/`login_chatgpt_device_code()` is not covered by `login_timeout_s` (which per the table bounds only `handle.wait()`), and nothing at all bounds the `sq auth logout` path — its runtime spawn and `logout()` call are absent from both the D7 table and the Failure Modes table. A hung runtime during login or logout blocks the CLI command indefinitely (Ctrl-C is only handled for login, per the "Timeout or cancellation mid-turn" row's turn scope). The design's own standard — every new I/O path enumerated with an explicit handling strategy — is met for the turn path and status, but not for logout, and only partially for login. Fix: state that `codex.account_timeout_s` (or a dedicated key) also bounds runtime start for login, and add a logout row to the Failure Modes table (including logout when no `auth.json` exists and SDK error during logout).

findings.title: Architecture alignment: auth model deviation is explicit, minimal, and correctly scoped
findings.description: The architecture (100-arch.orchestration-v2.md, "Authentication Patterns") states squadron does not unify authentication. This slice adds `InteractiveLogin` to the shared `providers/auth.py` layer, which is net-new relative to that document, but the design dedicates a section to arguing it is an optional capability implemented by one strategy, delegates entirely to the Codex runtime, stores no credentials, and leaves the architecture text accurate — with a named trigger for updating the architecture if a second provider adopts it. This is the right way to handle a documented extension point rather than a hidden boundary violation.

findings.title: Dependency directions and string-dispatch ban are respected
findings.description: Both new Protocols live in the shared provider layer (`providers/base.py`, `providers/auth.py`) and are consumed by CLI/doctor — dependencies point inward, matching the architecture's "core engine never depends on provider internals" invariant. `openai_codex` is imported only inside functions in `runtime.py`, `login.py`, and `agent.py`, so the module graph imports cleanly without the extra and the provider still registers (satisfying the architecture's provider implementation requirements). All new dispatch is capability-based (`isinstance(strategy, InteractiveLogin)`, `isinstance(provider, ExtraRequirement)`), consistent with slice 128's ban on profile-name/auth-type string comparisons, and the technical requirements pin this with a check.

findings.title: Slice-plan scope is fully carried; nothing assigned is dropped and nothing unassigned is added
findings.description: Every element of the slice-plan entry 129 maps to the design: port to `openai_codex` (Part A), bundled-binary-first with PATH fallback (D2), optional extra (D1), effort via `ReasoningEffort` closing #171 (D5), token usage (D6 — note the design uses the verified `TurnResult.usage` surface from SDK 0.159.3 rather than the plan's conditional `ThreadTokenUsageUpdated` phrasing, which is the more accurate form), install-hint error / doctor row / model-list marker / README (Part B), `sq auth login` browser + `--device-code`, `sq auth logout`, and email/plan in `sq auth status` (Part C). The plan's smoke test appears as walkthrough step 6. Exclusions (no squadron token store, no `login_api_key`, no streaming/tool plumbing changes, no `AuthStrategy` Protocol change) are all either things the plan leaves out or decisions the plan explicitly delegates. The three new config timeout keys are justified by the failure-mode table, not speculative abstraction.

findings.title: D-numbering is out of order in Technical Decisions
findings.description: D9 ("Extra missing" signal) appears before D8 ("Turn result is checked, not trusted"). Purely cosmetic; no content issue.
